correctness.rationale: For an equiangular polygon the area of each consecutive vertex triangle is one half of the product of the two adjacent side lengths times sin(2pi/n). Equal areas therefore force the exact two-step recurrence on side lengths. Odd cycles collapse to one length; even cycles alternate two lengths and close because each parity class of edge directions is a complete regular root-of-unity set. The area formula follows from a two-mode Fourier representation of the edge sequence, with mixed terms cancelling. The fixed-perimeter deficit and central-symmetry parity are direct exact consequences.
risks: The finite checker is only diagnostic and does not replace the all-n proof.

value.rationale: Equal-area polygons form a named affine-geometric class with nontrivial moduli, and equiangular polygons are a canonical Euclidean class. Determining their exact intersection is therefore a natural complete classification. The result is strengthened by a sharp fixed-perimeter area identity and a modulo-four central-symmetry transition, giving structural and quantitative information rather than a routine special value.
risks: The result is confined to the equiangular Euclidean slice and does not address the broader moduli connectedness problem.
